case-folder.text: Create a folder for the case, `~/{{caseDir}}`, with the subfolder `{{evidence}}` – with **one** command.
case-folder.hint: `mkdir -p` creates every folder along the way in one go.

copy-log.text: Secure the evidence: copy `~/{{documents}}/server.log` to `~/{{caseDir}}/{{evidence}}/`. The original must stay where it is.
copy-log.hint: Copy with `cp`, not `mv` – a detective never moves the evidence from the crime scene.

errors.text: Save every line with `ERROR` from the log in the file `~/{{caseDir}}/{{errorsFile}}`.
errors.hint: `grep` finds the lines and `>` sends them to a file instead of the screen.

count-warnings.text: How many warnings are there? Count the lines with `WARN` – in upper or lower case – and write the number as the first line of the report `~/{{caseDir}}/{{caseReport}}`.
count-warnings.hint: `grep -i` ignores upper and lower case, and `wc -l` counts the lines. Connect them with a pipe and finish with `>`.

first-error.text: When did the trouble start? Add **the first** error line to the report – without overwriting the number that is already there.
first-error.hint: `head -n 1` takes only the first line. `>>` adds to the end of the file, while `>` overwrites it.

times.text: Add **only the times** of all the errors to the report, one per line and sorted from the latest to the earliest.
times.hint: The fields of the log are separated by spaces, and the time is field 2: `cut -d' ' -f2`. `sort -r` sorts backwards. Build a pipe from `grep` through `cut` and `sort` and finish with `>>`.

show-report.text: Case solved! Show the whole report in the terminal and check that everything is there.
